claim.why_it_matters: Every row on the page is flattened to one level (no   indentation, unlike pages 726, 728 and 730), so sub-items are detached from their parent element: 'Literal option' and 'Literal can be figurative constant' no longer say which clause they qualify, and the two 'Computer-name' / 'Empty paragraph may be specified' rows no longer read as children of SOURCE-COMPUTER vs OBJECT-COMPUTER. Informative Appendix B table; no counts or module codes are wrong.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of page 729 (XVII-21) prints the ELEMENT column as a nested hierarchy: rows under ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, Configuration Section, SOURCE-COMPUTER, OBJECT-COMPUTER and SPECIAL-NAMES are indented one step; STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2/NATIVE/Implementor-name/Literal option are indented a further step under ALPHABET clause; 'Literal can be figurative constant' is indented under CURRENCY SIGN clause; IS mnemonic-name, ON STATUS and OFF STATUS options are indented under Implementor-name clause; and both 'If implementor-name is switch...' rows are indented one step further under IS mnemonic-name option. The transcription of page 729 renders every row at one flat level with no   prefixes, while the same table on adjacent pages (e.g. page 730: ' SELECT clause', '  OPTIONAL phrase', '   Input file') encodes the hierarchy. The parent-child relation is information the page carries (which clause 'Literal option' or 'Literal can be figurative constant' qualifies, which paragraph each 'Computer-name'/'Empty paragraph' row belongs to), and it is lost. Row order, text and all 2ND/3RD STD codes and Z flags match the print, so the defect is structural only, in an informative appendix table. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as stated. One detail to add: the print also places 'SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clause' at the same indent as ON/OFF STATUS (one step deeper than the other SPECIAL-NAMES clauses), and 'If implementor-name is switch, condition-name may be specified' is indented under IS mnemonic-name option like its 'must' sibling; a fix should restore   levels matching the print for every row on the page.
